messages:
Matt SRE: Heads up — we're seeing a ~7k->12k rps spike to /v1/embed.grpc on the edge, mostly tiny gRPC probe requests. KV cache miss rate jumped to ~95%, tail latencies spiked and 502s from origin increased.
Sam Ops: I see the same in dashboards. Traffic fingerprint: lots of unique session ids, User-Agent 'grpc-prober/1.2' repeated. ASN concentration in a few ranges.
Ellie SecEng: Sounds like an active probe/amplification. Can we short-circuit at the edge? Quick per-route rate limit + a WAF deny on that UA?
Matt SRE: Applying temporary rate-limit now. Pushing config: {"route":"/v1/embed.grpc","rate_limit":2000,"burst":500} — will monitor effects.
DeployBot: Rate limit rule applied to route /v1/embed.grpc by Matt SRE at 2026-03-20T09:12:47Z
Sam Ops: Also pushed a WAF rule to block UA regex /grpc-prober/ and drop requests with payload_size < 64 bytes.
Leah CS: Any customer impact we should proactively communicate? Are legitimate embedding jobs affected?
Matt SRE: Minimal 429s seen for a handful of very high-throughput customers; most clients unaffected. We'll notify top-10 embeddings customers with an advisory.
Jorge EngInfra: Origin KV cache thrash indicates probes cycling keys. Enabling prefix caching and bumping embedding response TTL to 5m to reduce origin load.
Ellie SecEng: Recommend blocking offending ASNs at the edge and blackholing the worst offenders temporarily. Can you list the ASNs?
Sam Ops: Top offending ASNs observed: 12345, 67890, 13579. I'm applying edge blocklist entries for those ranges.
Matt SRE: ASN blocklist deployed. Monitoring metrics now.
DeployBot: Edge blocklist updated by Sam Ops at 2026-03-20T09:18:03Z
Ellie SecEng: Open action items for post-incident: (1) add this UA and ASN signatures to IDS rules, (2) update runbook detection thresholds for gRPC probes, (3) audit RBAC for who can edit WAF/rules, (4) ensure audit logs capture these changes and ship to long-term storage.
Matt SRE: Created follow-up ticket INF-4527 with the mitigation steps and owners. Also request a KMS access log check — confirm edge signing keys weren't abused; consider rotation if anything suspicious.
Jorge EngInfra: I'll pull KMS access and key usage logs now. Note: rotating edge signing keys needs a deploy window; prefer confirm compromise before rotating.
Sam Ops: Scheduling a postmortem for tomorrow 10:00 PT, inviting Sec, SRE, Infra, and CS.
Leah CS: I'll draft the customer advisory: concise summary, mitigations we applied, expected impact, and guidance (no action needed unless you see persistent 429s). Will attach to INF-4527.
Ellie SecEng: Also request a quick RBAC audit for WAF/edit permissions in the last 90 days. If wide, we'll tighten to Sec + SRE leads.
Matt SRE: Agreed. Proposal: keep temporary rate limit in place for 6h and cache TTL at 5m for 24h, then re-evaluate. Any objections?
Sam Ops: No objections, metrics are trending in the right direction.
DeployBot: Incident annotated: mitigation=rate-limit,waf-block,asn-block,cache-ttl at 2026-03-20T09:25:11Z
Ellie SecEng: Good. Postmortem deliverables: runbook updates, IDS signatures, RBAC tightening, audit log retention increase, KMS access review. Assign owners inside INF-4527.
Leah CS: Customer comms draft uploaded to INF-4527 and CC'd to legal for sign-off.
Matt SRE: Thanks all. We'll keep live mitigations for another hour while we confirm stability, then remove ASN blocks and roll rate limits back.
Sam Ops: Metrics update: traffic down to baseline, cache miss back to ~12% — holding for 30m.
Matt SRE: Final update: spike subsided. Removed temporary ASN blocks and reduced rate limits to baseline. Follow-ups remain in INF-4527 for audit, RBAC, KMS checks, and runbook updates.
